extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-level publication criteria that authors must satisfy for a manuscript to be considered by PLOS ONE, covering scope, originality, technical quality, reporting, ethics, and data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: The study presents the results of primary scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate primary scientific research and welcomes submissions in any applied discipline that contribute to scientific knowledge. The journal will not consider secondary literature, certain article types, or purely theoretical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit exclusions: Reviews; Case studies (contemporary or historical); Study protocols; Hypothesis or proposal papers; Letters, commentaries, or essays; Opinion pieces; Policy papers; Any other type of secondary literature; Monographs; Purely theoretical research (such as pure mathematics). Occasional commissioned Collection Reviews/Overviews are only accepted when solicited. Article types PLOS ONE will consider: Systematic reviews (only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling of literature — see submission guidelines); Submissions describing methods, software, databases, or other tools (if they follow appropriate reporting guidelines — see submission guidelines); Qualitative research (only if it adheres to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines — see submission guidelines); Studies reporting negative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE does not accept studies already published, in whole or in part, in the peer-reviewed literature, nor submissions that are currently under consideration elsewhere. Figures must be original and not previously published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions/notes: Manuscripts deposited in preprint servers (e.g., arXiv) or published in a thesis, and work presented at conferences, may be considered. For replication studies or work very similar to previous work, authors must provide a sound scientific rationale and clearly reference and discuss existing literature; submissions that are derivative without adequate justification will likely be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments must be conducted rigorously with appropriate controls and replication, and all analyses (including statistics) must meet high technical standards and be described in enough detail to allow reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample sizes should be large enough to produce robust results where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments. (Implied: adherence to discipline-specific reporting and methodological best practices.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.description: The data presented in the manuscript must support the conclusions drawn; interpretations that are unjustified or inappropriate are grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Possible implications may be discussed but must be clearly identified as hypotheses rather than conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts must be written clearly, correctly, and unambiguously in standard English because PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that do not meet language standards may be rejected. If language is difficult to understand or includes many errors, authors may be asked to seek independent editorial help prior to revision; such services can be found via searches for 'scientific editing service' or 'manuscript editing service.'

rubrics_metrics.name: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted to the highest ethical standards; PLOS ONE may apply standards that are more stringent than local rules and reserves the right to reject submissions that do not meet ethical expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval from the relevant body is required for studies involving: humans (live or tissue), including observational or survey-based studies or those with personal data; animals (live or tissue), including observational studies; non-commercial cell lines; field sampling; and work with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. Publication ethics: PLOS ONE is a COPE member and follows COPE's Code of Conduct and Best Practice Guidelines; authors are expected to follow best practices on authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. For more details see Editorial Policies and Submission Guidelines; queries or concerns may be directed to the editorial office (plosone@plos.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.description: Results must be reported rigorously following discipline-specific reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability and deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow standards/practices for data deposition in publicly available resources for data types such as gene sequences, microarray expression, structural studies, and similar data. Failure to comply with community standards for reporting or data deposition may result in rejection. See the submission guidelines and the PLOS ONE data availability policy for more information.
